text: Withdrawals are capped by a daily limit of 5000.00 per account, rejected with 'daily-limit' when exceeded.
The daily withdrawal counter is never reset, so the 'daily' limit is in practice a lifetime limit for the ledger instance.
The daily limit counts only the withdrawn amount, not the fee, and is checked after the funds check.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00.
The 1% fee is rounded up to the next cent (ceiling) with a small epsilon.
A withdrawal is rejected as 'insufficient-funds' unless the balance covers the amount plus the fee; overdrafts are not allowed.
Transfers and split payments are rejected as 'insufficient-funds' if the sender's balance would go negative.
Cent conversion adds a 1e-7 epsilon before rounding to compensate for floating-point error.
A repeated transaction id returns success without doing anything and without checking that the retry has the same account, amount or operation type.
Transaction ids are global across all accounts and operation types, held in one set for the ledger's lifetime.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry of an accepted id with an invalid amount (or an empty recipient list) is rejected instead of treated as a duplicate.
A transaction id is only marked as seen on success, so a failed operation can be retried with the same id and later succeed.
Accounts are created implicitly on first use by any operation, including withdrawals and as the source of transfers or splits.
Querying an unknown account returns a balance of 0 and an empty history rather than an error.
Validation rejects NaN and non-positive values with 'invalid-amount' but accepts Infinity.
Errors are returned as a result object with string reason codes rather than thrown.
The exchange rate must be positive or the foreign deposit is rejected with 'invalid-amount'.
The foreign amount is multiplied by the rate without first rounding the foreign amount itself.
A foreign deposit that converts to zero cents is rejected with 'amount-too-small'.
A foreign deposit is recorded as a plain 'deposit' entry with no record of the original currency amount or rate.
The withdrawal and its fee are debited together and recorded as a single 'withdrawal' entry whose amount includes the fee.
Interest takes the rate as a percentage and computes simple (non-compounded) interest on the current balance.
Interest is rounded down (floor) to the cent, with an epsilon.
Interest that rounds to zero returns success without a history entry and without marking the transaction id as seen.
Interest requires a positive rate and positive days, and allows fractional days.
A split with no recipients is rejected with 'no-recipients'.
When a split amount does not divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first recipients in list order.
Split payments allow duplicate recipients and allow the sender to be a recipient.
History entries store amounts as unsigned decimal currency units (not cents), with direction given only by the entry kind.
Rejected operations are not recorded in history.
